en: The Accomplishment of Non-duality. Om. Homage to the glorious Vajrasattva!
Having bowed my head to the Lord, who is naturally luminous, the omniscient one born from the three realms of existence, the bestower of the fruits of desired aims through the vajra—
[I shall explain this] without regard for place, time, lunar day, weekday, asterism, or mandala.
I shall explain the supreme *sādhana* of Vajrasattva in brief. (1)

For a yogi who does not realize the ultimate reality, success will not be attained even in hundreds of millions of eons through observances, vows, fasts, the recitation of mantras, or meditative contemplations. ||2||

The mantra practitioner should constantly worship himself with the flute, vajra, water, seed-syllables, and so forth, which arise within the nostrils, through the meditations on the principles (tattvas). ||3||
The knower of yoga should always worship his mother, sister, daughter, and niece by means of the method of wisdom and skillful means.
One should always honor women who are deficient in a limb, low-born, artisans, or even outcaste women, by means of the manifestation of the vajra of knowledge.
These are the seed-syllable mantras of reality: Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ.
For by whatever fierce karma sentient beings are bound, by that very same means they are liberated from the bondage of existence. (6)
Every day, one should perform the daily rites and worship the divine deities born of the five families with lamps and other offerings, along with milk and substances originating from the universe.
With eyes wide open like blossoming flowers and a face always smiling, the minister, having fixed his mind upon perfect enlightenment, should meditate on the ocean of gnosis. (8)
O Vajradhṛk, however many stable and moving entities exist here in this abode of the three realms, all these should be viewed through the yoga of reality. 9.

Furthermore, whatever proponents of other doctrines exist who are established through various distinctions of sectarian marks, they too must not be disparaged here, for they are the miraculous manifestations of Vajrasattva. (10)
Having rendered all phenomena equal in taste through their emergence from selflessness, the mantra-practitioner should constantly meditate upon the body as naturally stainless. (11)

The Lord is worshipped with perfumes, garlands, and the like, as well as with garments, incense, and food offerings; likewise, He is worshipped with songs, instrumental music, and dances, along with various other means.
One should not perform painful mental exercises, nor fasting, nor ritual acts; here there is neither bathing, nor purification, nor even the avoidance of village customs.
One should not even pay homage to those made of wood, stone, or clay;
one should always perform worship with a body that is perfectly composed in concentration.
One should worship the Holder of the Vajra with five lamps prepared from substances such as feces and urine, mixed with flies and vomit, and consecrated [with mantras]. ||15||

A woman should worship the deity residing within her own body with self-arisen flowers accompanied by milk, which originate from the universe, while maintaining the contemplation of the true principles (tattva). 16.
One may take the property of others, indulge with the wives of others, speak false words, and even cause all Buddhas to be slain. ||17||
One should not construct stupas made of stone, clay, or other materials, nor take delight in books or mandalas, even in a dream, through the actions of body, speech, or mind. (18)
The knower of mantras, Vajrasattva himself, dwells there in person; therefore, one should not feel disgust toward any objects whatsoever. (19)

A mantra practitioner who is fully concentrated should never entertain the conceptual distinction between those who may be approached and those who may not, nor likewise between what is edible and what is inedible, or what is drinkable and what is undrinkable. (20)

One who possesses vital breath, knows the secret reality, and is the cause of accomplishment should cause all living beings, who have arisen from Vairocana and are produced from him, to enjoy [the offerings] for the sake of attaining siddhi.
Women born from all castes are not to be despised;
they are that very Blessed Lady Prajñā herself, who has assumed a form through conventional reality (saṃvṛti). ||22||
For one endowed with non-dual knowledge, no specific lunar day, nor asterism, nor the rule of fasting is prescribed; for such a person, the accomplishment of the Sugata arises. //23//
What is the use of saying more here? Whatever is perceived by you should all be viewed through the application of reality by one who knows reality. (24)
The knower of yoga should always consume the lamp made from elephant, horse, donkey, cow, and camel, mixed with the great lamp produced from dog. 25.
The knower of yoga should not form an attachment even to a single [object]; the ocean of existence is to be meditated upon through the yoga of equanimity of mind. ||26||
One should contemplate its arising, persistence, and cessation as being unassociated with ordinary beings; for its cyclic existence consists of nothing other than dissolution and emergence. (27)
The Blessed One who possesses the vajra is designated as day, and wisdom as night;
by meditating in this way, the yogi shall attain swift accomplishment. ||28||
That unmanifest form which resides within all sentient beings—the supreme reality—is attained from the mouth of the Guru; of this there is no doubt. (29)
Non-abiding nirvana, signless, without abode, all-pervading among all sentient beings—this is supreme perfect enlightenment, the ultimate state. ||30||
Thinking thus, the wise yogi who constantly meditates upon it will certainly attain perfection; of this there is no doubt, even if he is a man of meager merit. (31)
There is nothing higher than the teacher in the three worlds, including all things mobile and immobile; by his grace, various accomplishments are attained by the wise in manifold ways. (32)
Vajrasattva, who is all-knowing and saluted by all the Buddhas, is the supreme deity of the Ācāryas; he should be worshipped with diligent effort. (33)
He, whose nature is suchness, for the sake of favoring the world, relies upon form and abides conventionally upon the seat of yoga. //34//
This death is a conceptual construction; it is not an entity among all things.
It is destroyed by conceptualization through the mental proliferations of ordinary beings. ||35||

This manual of practice, which arises from the sequence of the Svādhiṣṭhāna, has emerged from the lotus-face of Śrī Lakṣmī; it has issued forth from the venerable Madoḍiyāna, reached the Mahāyoga-pīṭhas, and contains within its core the essential reality of all Yoga Tantras.
Thus it is concluded.
